alt: Paper 2 lasts 2 hours 40 minutes for 110 marks (30% of the A-level). Section A, translation into Urdu, has 20 marks and 30 minutes; each of the two works responses has 45 marks and about 1 hour 5 minutes. Section A is marked in 20 one-mark chunks, and verb and adjective endings must be correct.
caption: Translation first, then two 45-mark essays; endings are never treated as spelling.

alt: Three literary texts (Aangan آنگن, novel, Khadija Mastur, 1999; Patras Ke Mazameen پطرس کے مضامین, essays, 2011, five essays prescribed; Bisaat بساط, play, Baseer Kazmi, 1987) and three films (Bin Roye بن روئے, 2015; Baaghban باغبان, 2003; Bajrangi Bhaijaan بجرنگی بھائی جان, 2015).
caption: Three texts and three films; the films are given by name and year only.

alt: Each studied work is prepared from five angles: form and technique, key themes and issues, characterisation, plot structure, and social and cultural setting, then connected to the qualification’s four themes for AO4.
caption: Revise each work from all five angles and link it to the wider themes.

after: ## Worked example: structuring a works response
alt: A works essay states a position, supports it with two or three specific scenes or lines, and closes by connecting the issue to its wider social theme, earning AO3 through precise language and AO4 through cultural context. Chronological retelling is the trap.
caption: Position, evidence, cultural connection: argue, do not retell.

alt: The two allowed combinations of works essays: two literary-text essays (Section B twice), or one literary-text essay and one film essay (Sections B and C). Two film essays, or three extended responses, are not allowed.
caption: Two texts, or a text and a film: never two films, never three essays.
